note_on_method: Every court count and every surface below comes from that park's own page on cityofmadison.com, in the block the City heads "Tennis & Pickleball" or, at Garner Park, "Pickleball". Every address comes from the City's pickleball courts list. Where a park page says nothing about its courts beyond that block — and several say very little about the park at all — this page says nothing either. Nobody working on this has played on these courts.

slots.description:
Two courts on asphalt, on a 6.47-acre neighbourhood park on Madison's west side. The City describes Bordner as "the perfect location for nearby residents, families, and people of all ages", with basketball courts, an open field for a pick-up game of soccer, a playground, and the tennis courts that carry the pickleball lines. That last detail is the one to hold on to: like nineteen of Madison's twenty outdoor pickleball venues, this is a tennis court with pickleball markings on it rather than a pickleball court, and the City is explicit about what that means in practice.

Bordner sits in the largest group in Madison's pickleball inventory: fourteen of the city's twenty outdoor venues carry exactly two courts, and this is one of them. That distribution is the real shape of pickleball here — not a few big complexes but a two-court pair painted onto tennis courts in park after park, spread across every side of the city. It is why the interesting question in Madison is rarely how many courts a venue has and usually what it is made of and whether it is shared, both of which the City answers.
slots.getting_there: 5610 Elder Pl., Madison, WI 53705, which the Census geocoder matched cleanly to Madison city, Dane County. The City publishes nothing about parking at any of its pickleball venues, and on a park of this size — under seven acres, in a residential street grid — the realistic expectation is street parking rather than a lot. Nothing on the park page contradicts that, and nothing on it confirms it either.
slots.what_to_expect: Two courts, shared with tennis, played over a tennis net that Madison notes is "about 2\" taller than a standard pickleball net". Individuals play first come, first served; the City's one caveat citywide is that leagues and lessons must reserve in advance, and it does not publish where those bookings appear. Lighting is not verified here — Madison marks its one lit venue and says nothing about the rest — so plan for daylight. With two courts and a neighbourhood catchment, this is a venue for a pair or two rather than a group. What the City does not publish for Bordner is as telling as what it does: no restrooms, no shelter, no parking, no hours. The record here is a court count, a surface, an address and an acreage, and this page will not turn that into a description of what a Tuesday evening feels like.

The pickleball is three courts of that, striped onto tennis courts, which is a fair illustration of how the sport sits in Madison: distributed across the park system rather than concentrated in a facility.

Elver is the outlier that shows how little park size predicts court count. At 250.82 acres it is the largest community park Madison Parks runs, and its three courts put it level with Tenney and Warner and behind Brittingham's four and Garner's six — two parks a fraction of its size. Across the city, twenty outdoor venues hold forty-eight courts between them, an average of just under two and a half each, and Elver is almost exactly average on a park more than forty times the median size.

Door Creek was first acquired in 1990 and got its master plan in 2008. Alongside the courts the park carries a reservable shelter, a large playground, basketball courts, hiking trails and multipurpose fields, and it backs onto Dane County's Blooming Grove Drumlins Natural Resource Area. New for the 2025-26 winter, the City added an ice rink and a staffed pavilion renting cross-country skis, skates and snowshoes.
slots.getting_there:
7035 Littlemore Dr., Madison, WI 53718, on the far east side in the Door Creek neighbourhood. This address is the reason the venue took until 4 September 2026 to appear here: the US Census address file has no record of it, and until that date this site had exactly one address resolver. It now consults OpenStreetMap where the Census has nothing and accepts the answer only at house-number level, which this address meets. The county and postcode published here come from OpenStreetMap rather than the Census.

The City lists five alternate access points for the park — 6901 Bluff Point Drive, 851 Harrington Drive, 7202 Cottage Grove Rd., 625 Highcliff Trail and a point between 533 and 601 Highcliff Trail — which is worth knowing in a park this size. It publishes nothing about parking, here or at any Madison venue.
slots.what_to_expect: Eight shared courts is the most pickleball capacity outdoors anywhere in Madison, and the practical consequence is that this is the venue least likely to have you waiting. The courts are tennis courts striped for pickleball, so the net you play over is a tennis net, which the City notes is "about 2\" taller than a standard pickleball net". Individuals play first come, first served; leagues and lessons must reserve in advance. Lighting is not stated, and neither are nets — bring a paddle and expect to bring a net.

slots.description:
Six courts on asphalt on the west side, behind Hilldale Mall, in a 20-acre park. The City's line reads "Courts: 6, asphalt" under "Tennis & Pickleball", and the park description fills in what they are: "six tennis courts, three with lighting". Read the two together and this is six tennis courts striped for pickleball, of which three carry lights — but the lighting statement is made about the tennis courts in the park's prose and not in the court line the City uses to mark its lit pickleball venues, so lighting is left unverified here rather than published on an inference.

The City also carries a dated note on this park's page: "Update October 20, 2025: West court construction is substantially completed and courts are open for play!" That is the most recent statement Madison makes about any of its pickleball surfaces, and it is why the courts you find here are newer than most in the city.

slots.what_to_expect: Six shared courts, recently rebuilt on the west side, first come and first served for individuals; leagues and lessons reserve in advance. Three of the park's six tennis courts have lighting according to the park description, so evening play may be possible — but the City does not say it about the pickleball courts in the line where it says it elsewhere, so treat that as the park's own words rather than as a verified fact on this page. The park also holds a large reservable shelter, a climbing-net playground, a free-to-use disc golf basket, a concrete ping pong table and a checkers table, and the Jeff Erlanger sprayground, which opened in 2025.
